articleSummary: A 55-year-old woman from Chongqing, China, has died after contracting the H5N6 bird flu, marking a significant human case in the region. As the mosquito population grows, vigilance in prevention and early medical intervention is crucial to manage the potential dual threat of these mosquito-borne diseases.

articleHeadline: HIV in India: Injecting drug use drives new infections and deaths
articleSummary: Punjab recorded 6,785 new HIV infections in 2024, marking a significant public health concern as it holds the second-highest national tally after Bihar. Additionally, HIV transmissions from injecting drug users are the primary driver of new infections, while heterosexual contact with non-regular partners accounts for approximately 17%. The mortality rate has also escalated, with deaths increasing from 430 in 2020 to 961 in 2024. In contrast, neighboring states like Haryana and Rajasthan reported lower infection rates, with figures around 2,900 and 4,000 respectively. In response to the crisis, Punjab has implemented public health measures, distributing over 6 million needles and syringes and enrolling nearly 11,000 injecting drug users in opioid substitution therapy during 2024-25.

articleSummary: Five individuals in Yanggu County, Shandong Province, have been diagnosed with cutaneous anthrax, prompting immediate quarantine measures and containment efforts by local authorities.
